cohort: Pregnant women with and without adenomyosis (7,608 with adenomyosis and 566,153 without adenomyosis)
finding: Pregnant women with adenomyosis had a 52.1% increased risk of experiencing obstetric complications, including IUGR, preterm delivery, cesarean delivery, hypertensive disorders, placental abruption, and spontaneous abortion, compared to pregnant women without adenomyosis.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was slightly more common in pregnant women with adenomyosis compared to those without adenomyosis (OR = 1.099, p = 0.046).
